title: Distinguish references and moves
description: You can compare references to named objects with references to temporary values. std::move permits a move operation by changing how its argument is treated.

steps.description: x is a named object. lr refers to x, while rr and rr2 bind to temporary values.
The string concatenation creates a temporary string. rs binds to that result.
std::move is a cast rather than a transfer by itself. Initializing t from that expression invokes the string's move behavior.
The moved-from string s remains valid with an unspecified state. You should keep that distinction when reading the stream expression.
